title: Implementing Secure Identity Federation in AWS using SAML and Okta
objectives: Configure AWS IAM to accept SAML assertions from Okta
Verify successful authentication and attribute mapping
Troubleshoot common issues with SAML federation
prerequisites: Basic understanding of AWS IAM and identity management
Familiarity with Okta as an identity provider
Knowledge of SAML protocol and its applications in cloud security

mission_brief.briefing: Your team has been tasked with implementing secure identity federation between Aegis Logistics' Okta environment and AWS. Your goal is to configure IAM to accept SAML assertions from Okta, ensuring seamless authentication and authorization for users.
rules_of_engagement: Use only publicly available tools and services
Avoid modifying or deleting existing resources without approval
Document all configuration changes and testing results

content.concept: Secure identity federation using SAML protocol enables organisations to manage access to cloud resources while maintaining control over user identities. By integrating Okta with AWS IAM, users can authenticate once in Okta and access multiple AWS services without needing separate credentials.
content.walkthrough: To implement secure identity federation, follow these steps: Configure the Identity Provider (IdP) in Okta to issue SAML assertions. Create a Service Provider (SP) entity in AWS IAM to accept these assertions. Define attribute mappings between Okta user attributes and AWS IAM roles.
checkpoints: Verify Okta configuration for SAML protocol
Ensure correct attribute mapping between Okta and AWS IAM
Test successful authentication and authorization of users
common_mistakes: Incorrectly configuring the SP entity in AWS IAM
Failing to map attributes correctly between Okta and AWS IAM
Not testing authentication and authorization thoroughly

lab.setup: Create an Okta tenant with SAML protocol enabled. Create an AWS account with the necessary permissions for identity management.
steps: Configure the IdP in Okta to issue SAML assertions
Create a new SP entity in AWS IAM and configure it to accept SAML assertions from Okta
Define attribute mappings between Okta user attributes and AWS IAM roles
Test successful authentication and authorization of users using the Okta Test User
Verify that access is denied for users who do not have necessary permissions
safety: Be cautious when modifying IAM roles and users
Regularly back up your AWS account and Okta tenant configurations
Follow all security best practices for cloud identity management

elite_competence.role_simulation: Play the role of a malicious user attempting to exploit vulnerabilities in the SAML federation between Okta and AWS IAM.

bug_injection.description: Inject a bug into the SAML assertion issued by Okta, causing it to be rejected by AWS IAM due to incorrect attribute mapping
bug_injection.bad_state: The SAML assertion should contain the correct attribute mapping between Okta user attributes and AWS IAM roles

interrogation_questions: What would happen if the SAML assertion issued by Okta contained incorrect attribute mapping?
How can you troubleshoot issues with SAML federation between Okta and AWS IAM?
Can you describe a scenario where a malicious user could exploit vulnerabilities in the SAML federation?

accessibility.alt_text_summary: This lesson covers implementing secure identity federation in AWS using SAML and Okta, a critical aspect of cloud security.

resume_bullets: Configured SAML protocol between Okta and AWS IAM for secure identity federation
Verified successful authentication and authorization of users using the Okta Test User
Troubleshooted common issues with SAML federation and attribute mapping
